In the Komlos construction, one step is to consider truncated functions (see here) and I wondered if there is already some API for this. There is docs#ProbabilityTheory.truncation but we can't use it here since that only works for real-valued functions.
I think that similar arguments to the one in the Komlos proof appear quite often, should there be a general truncation API (for functions into a normed space)? Or does something like that already exist and I'm just overlooking it?
I think a general truncation definition could be useful. I don't think it exists.

As far as I can see we could define this abstractly for any f : A → B where we have only [Norm B] and [Zero B]. So perhaps a natural home would be Analysis/Normed/Truncation.lean.

The main question to decide is probably what we want the type of the value to truncate with to be, I suppose eitherℝ≥0 or ℝ. It might be nice to have trunc f val ≤ val without the assumption 0 ≤ val, but we only get that in the first case. But then one always has to cast to ℝ≥0 when one works with a value of type ℝ...
